citation.authors: Elmajnoun HK, Faris ME, Abdelrahim DN, Haris PI et al

cited_by.title: Fasting in Ramadan with diabetes or sickle cell

record.population: 5,554 adults with type 2 diabetes in 12 observational studies from Middle Eastern and Asian countries
record.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of before-and-after studies of Ramadan fasting
record.finding: HbA1c and fasting blood glucose were significantly lower after Ramadan than before it (heterogeneity high, about 93% and 81%); body weight did not change. The authors call the outcomes favourable and say effects of diet, activity and sleep need study. No study looked only at young adults.
record.note: No control group of non-fasters; people who choose to fast may be healthier. The studies were not in Black populations.
